# Metrics

**14 groups, A-N.** Each is independent: a group that fails records `error_<LETTER>` and the others still run, and a group whose sentinel key is already present is not recomputed, so groups can be added to a finished run without redoing the rest.

By default `A,B,E,J,K` run — the fast ones that need no R and no permutations.

```bash
combobatch metrics --config c.yaml --groups A,B,E,J,K
combobatch metrics --config c.yaml --groups all --force-groups F
```

## Reading a metric name

Metric keys carry **the column they were computed against**, taken from your `ColumnSpec` — the same group emits `r2_site` on one dataset and `r2_sequencing_run` on another. Nothing here has an opinion about what your columns are called.

That also means polarity depends on the column: a batch-keyed metric and a biology-keyed metric from the same group usually point in opposite directions. The polarity column below says which is which.

## The groups

| Group | Name | Cost | Default | Needs | Polarity |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **E** | Data quality | fast | yes | — | descriptive; no direction |
| **K** | NA retention | fast | yes | — | higher is better |
| **A** | PCA variance decomposition | moderate | yes | pca | lower is better for batch, higher for biology |
| **J** | Per-PC variance | fast | yes | pca | descriptive; no direction |
| **B** | Neighbourhood integration | slow | yes | pca | higher is better for batch mixing, higher for cLISI |
| **C** | Embedding structure | slow | no | pca, umap, tsne | lower dispersion and higher entropy are better |
| **D** | Distribution comparison | slow | no | — | lower is better |
| **G** | Graph connectivity | moderate | no | pca | higher is better |
| **H** | Pairwise distances | moderate | no | — | lower ratio for batch, higher for biology |
| **I** | WaterMelon score | very_slow | no | pca | higher is better for biology |
| **L** | Profile preservation | moderate | no | reference matrix, marker panel | higher is better, but saturates |
| **M** | Cross-batch rank agreement | moderate | no | marker panel | higher margin is better |
| **N** | Predictive validation | very_slow | no | — | higher is better, above the permutation null |
| **F** | Variance partition | very_slow | no | R | lower for batch, higher for biology |

### E — Data quality

Shape, batch balance, zero inflation, expression percentiles and per-cohort bimodality.

- **Sentinel key:** `n_samples`
- **Columns consumed:** batch, bio, cohort
- **Polarity:** descriptive; no direction
- **Cost:** fast
- **Citation:** Descriptive statistics; no single source.
- **Keys emitted** (30): `below_1_fraction_by_batch_max`, `below_1_fraction_by_batch_min`, `exp_max`, `exp_median`, `exp_min`, `exp_p01`, `exp_p05`, `exp_p25`, `exp_p75`, `exp_p95`, `exp_p99`, `exp_std`, `fraction_cohorts_bimodal`, `fraction_cohorts_zero_inflated_bimodal`, `fraction_genes_below_1`, `n_batches`, `n_bio_groups`, `n_cohorts`, `n_cohorts_bimodal`, `n_cohorts_zero_inflated_bimodal`, `n_genes`, `n_samples`, `n_samples_per_batch_max`, `n_samples_per_batch_median`, `n_samples_per_batch_min`, `n_samples_per_batch_sd`, `per_batch_median_cv`, `zero_fraction_by_batch_max`, `zero_fraction_by_batch_min`, `zero_fraction_global`

### K — NA retention

Genes and samples free of missing values after harmonization — the cheapest way to catch a method that silently destroyed the matrix.

- **Sentinel key:** `n_genes_noNA`
- **Columns consumed:** none
- **Polarity:** higher is better
- **Cost:** fast
- **Citation:** ComboBatch-specific integrity check; no external source.
- **Keys emitted** (8): `n_genes_allNA`, `n_genes_noNA`, `n_na_cells`, `n_samples_allNA`, `n_samples_noNA`, `pct_genes_noNA`, `pct_na_cells`, `pct_samples_noNA`

### A — PCA variance decomposition

How much of each principal component's variance each annotation column explains, plus a permutation-tested separability score.

- **Sentinel key:** `r2_{batch}`
- **Columns consumed:** batch, bio, cohort
- **Polarity:** lower is better for batch, higher for biology
- **Cost:** moderate
- **Citation:** Buttner et al. 2019, Nat Methods (PCR/PCReg); Teschendorff & Zhu 2011 (DSC).
- **Keys emitted** (18): `dsc_batch`, `dsc_pvalue_batch`, `pcr_batch`, `pcr_bio`, `pcr_cohort`, `r2_batch`, `r2_bio`, `r2_cohort`, `r2_pc10_batch`, `r2_pc1_batch`, `r2_pc2_batch`, `r2_pc3_batch`, `r2_pc4_batch`, `r2_pc5_batch`, `r2_pc6_batch`, `r2_pc7_batch`, `r2_pc8_batch`, `r2_pc9_batch`

### J — Per-PC variance

Share of total variance carried by each leading component.

- **Sentinel key:** `pct_var_pc1`
- **Columns consumed:** none
- **Polarity:** descriptive; no direction
- **Cost:** fast
- **Citation:** Standard PCA scree diagnostics.
- **Keys emitted** (11): `pct_var_cum_top10`, `pct_var_pc1`, `pct_var_pc10`, `pct_var_pc2`, `pct_var_pc3`, `pct_var_pc4`, `pct_var_pc5`, `pct_var_pc6`, `pct_var_pc7`, `pct_var_pc8`, `pct_var_pc9`

### B — Neighbourhood integration

kBET, iLISI/cLISI, silhouettes and cell mixing: whether batches blend locally while biology stays apart.

- **Sentinel key:** `kbet_acceptance_rate_{batch}`
- **Columns consumed:** batch, bio
- **Polarity:** higher is better for batch mixing, higher for cLISI
- **Cost:** slow
- **Citation:** Buttner et al. 2019, Nat Methods (kBET); Korsunsky et al. 2019, Nat Methods (LISI).
- **Keys emitted** (10): `asw_batch_batch`, `asw_batch_norm_batch`, `asw_bio_bio`, `asw_bio_norm_bio`, `clisi_mean_bio`, `cms_fraction_mixed_batch`, `cms_mean_batch`, `ilisi_mean_batch`, `ilisi_norm_batch`, `kbet_acceptance_rate_batch`

### C — Embedding structure

Centroid dispersion and local entropy of batch labels in UMAP and t-SNE space.

- **Sentinel key:** `umap_centroid_disp_{batch}`
- **Columns consumed:** batch
- **Polarity:** lower dispersion and higher entropy are better
- **Cost:** slow
- **Citation:** McInnes et al. 2018, arXiv (UMAP); van der Maaten & Hinton 2008, JMLR (t-SNE).
- **Keys emitted** (6): `tsne_centroid_disp_batch`, `tsne_entropy_mean_batch`, `tsne_entropy_norm_batch`, `umap_centroid_disp_batch`, `umap_entropy_mean_batch`, `umap_entropy_norm_batch`

### D — Distribution comparison

Pairwise Kolmogorov-Smirnov distances between groups, cohort effects within a batch, and per-gene coefficient of variation.

- **Sentinel key:** `ks_mean_D_{batch}`
- **Columns consumed:** batch, cohort
- **Polarity:** lower is better
- **Cost:** slow
- **Citation:** Massey 1951, JASA (Kolmogorov-Smirnov).
- **Keys emitted** (8): `ks_cohort_within_batch_frac_sig`, `ks_cohort_within_batch_mean_D`, `ks_frac_sig_batch`, `ks_frac_sig_cohort`, `ks_mean_D_batch`, `ks_mean_D_cohort`, `per_gene_batch_mean_cv_batch`, `per_gene_batch_mean_cv_cohort`

### G — Graph connectivity

Whether each biology group forms a single connected kNN component rather than one island per batch.

- **Sentinel key:** `graph_connectivity_{bio}`
- **Columns consumed:** bio
- **Polarity:** higher is better
- **Cost:** moderate
- **Citation:** Luecken et al. 2022, Nat Methods (scIB graph connectivity).
- **Keys emitted** (1): `graph_connectivity_bio`

### H — Pairwise distances

Average within-group against between-group Euclidean distance in full gene space.

- **Sentinel key:** `dist_ratio_{batch}`
- **Columns consumed:** batch, bio, cohort
- **Polarity:** lower ratio for batch, higher for biology
- **Cost:** moderate
- **Citation:** Standard cluster-separation statistic; see Luecken et al. 2022.
- **Keys emitted** (9): `avg_inter_dist_batch`, `avg_inter_dist_bio`, `avg_inter_dist_cohort`, `avg_intra_dist_batch`, `avg_intra_dist_bio`, `avg_intra_dist_cohort`, `dist_ratio_batch`, `dist_ratio_bio`, `dist_ratio_cohort`

### I — WaterMelon score

Information a Ward dendrogram recovers about each label, against a permutation null.

- **Sentinel key:** `wm_{batch}`
- **Columns consumed:** batch, bio
- **Polarity:** higher is better for biology
- **Cost:** very_slow
- **Citation:** Ward 1963, JASA; permutation null as in Luecken et al. 2022.
- **Keys emitted** (6): `wm_batch`, `wm_bio`, `wm_mean_batch`, `wm_mean_bio`, `wm_ratio_bio_batch`, `wm_subsampled`

### L — Profile preservation

Within-cohort Spearman correlation of each gene before and after harmonization. Saturates at ~1.0 for any per-batch monotone transform, so read it as a guard rail, not a ranking.

- **Sentinel key:** `mk_rho_mean_all_genes`
- **Columns consumed:** cohort
- **Polarity:** higher is better, but saturates
- **Cost:** moderate
- **Citation:** ComboBatch-specific biology-preservation guard rail; see docs/METRICS.md.
- **Keys emitted** (18): `mk_is_self_reference`, `mk_n_cohorts_skipped_small`, `mk_n_cohorts_used`, `mk_n_genes_null`, `mk_n_panel_genes_used`, `mk_panel_coverage_frac`, `mk_rho_by_cohort`, `mk_rho_by_gene`, `mk_rho_frac_genes_above_0.9`, `mk_rho_marker_minus_hk`, `mk_rho_mean_all_genes`, `mk_rho_mean_by_cohort_mean`, `mk_rho_mean_housekeeping`, `mk_rho_mean_markers`, `mk_rho_median_all_genes`, `mk_rho_min_all_genes`, `mk_rho_n_cohorts_by_gene`, `mk_rho_p10_all_genes`

### M — Cross-batch rank agreement

Whether same-biology samples agree across batches more than different-biology ones. The margin is the discriminative signal.

- **Sentinel key:** `xb_rank_agree`

- **Polarity:** higher margin is better
- **Cost:** moderate
- **Citation:** ComboBatch-specific cross-batch discrimination score.
- **Keys emitted** (11): `xb_n_pairs_diff_bio`, `xb_n_pairs_same_bio`, `xb_n_panel_genes_used`, `xb_n_samples_used`, `xb_rank_agree`, `xb_rank_agree_by_bio`, `xb_rank_agree_median`, `xb_rank_agree_ratio`, `xb_rank_disagree_diffbio`, `xb_rank_disagree_diffbio_median`, `xb_subsampled`

### F — Variance partition

Per-gene variance attributed to each annotation column by a mixed model, via R's variancePartition.

- **Sentinel key:** `vp_median_{batch}`
- **Columns consumed:** batch, bio, cohort
- **Polarity:** lower for batch, higher for biology
- **Cost:** very_slow
- **Citation:** Hoffman & Schadt 2016, BMC Bioinformatics (variancePartition).
- **Keys emitted:** not enumerated here — this group needs R, and probing it would make this file differ between environments.

## Two caveats that change how these are read

**Group L saturates.** Its within-cohort correlation reaches exactly 1.0 for any per-gene monotone transform, which most linear harmonization methods are. It is a guard rail that catches a method destroying the biology, not a ranking that distinguishes good methods from better ones. Group M's margin carries the discriminative signal instead.

**Global and local metrics disagree, and both are needed.** In the source benchmark the two families were near-orthogonal (median Spearman r ≈ 0.009): a good PCA R² coexists comfortably with batches that remain separated locally. Reading only one family is how a method gets called good when it is not.

## Cost

`--skip-slow` drops every group marked `very_slow` and names each exclusion in the log with the flag that undoes it. `--force-groups` beats every exclusion, including an existing sentinel.
